text: An old wizard of the Empire who has spent longer giving counsel than most kingdoms have stood. He follows your faction leader from the first day of the campaign, and he will not stay dead for long.

Nobody at court remembers hiring him. He was simply there one morning, leaning on his staff by the war table, already correcting the maps.\\n\\nHe has outlived the generals who ignored him and quietly buried the ones who listened too late. Some say he trained at every College in Altdorf and was thrown out of each in turn. He says only that he has seen how this ends, and would rather it ended differently.

The men around him fight the way he taught them, whatever he holds.
Seven teachers, seven endings, and he took the best of each. What comes out is nobody's but his.
A thin shimmer, taught to him by a mage whose name no one else recalls.
The last arrow is always the one he saved for himself. He stopped saving it.
A flick of the wrist and the blade glances aside. He has practised it on worse than swords.
At the end of one world the Winds themselves held his sword arm. He remembers the grip.
One shot, then a hundred, then the sky goes dark with them.
He has been the last man standing. It taught him how to be the first one back up.
His body has healed from worse, many times. It still knows how.
Leather, steel, and a lesson from a swordsman who did not live to see the sequel.
He has learned to stretch the shimmer thin, across every rank that stands with him.
He has fought for days at the end of the world. One afternoon does not tire him.
A target seen sooner is a target already lost.
A broken shell is a lesson. He has learned to stitch it faster.
Aim for the buckle. The buckle is where armour ends.
He has loosed arrows at the end of every kind of world. The hand knows where to go.
A thin shimmer of the Winds holds in front of him.
He casts with one hand and cuts with the other, and has never found the two work apart.
He miscast once, at the worst possible moment, and the world ended a little early.
Every cut carries a little of the spell that guided it.
Scar over scar over scar. Little finds soft skin to bite.
He has been unmade by sorcery before. He remembers the shape of the hole.
Where he stands, broken shells knit again. The men near him feel it before they understand it.
He learned to charge from a knight who rode into the last sunset of a dying world.
Three kinds of rot are not enough.
He has watched Chaos corruption eat a world. He knows exactly where to plant it.
He has watched Khorne corruption eat a world. He knows exactly where to plant it.
He has watched Nurgle corruption eat a world. He knows exactly where to plant it.
He has watched Skaven corruption eat a world. He knows exactly where to plant it.
He has watched Slaanesh corruption eat a world. He knows exactly where to plant it.
He has watched Tzeentch corruption eat a world. He knows exactly where to plant it.
He has watched Vampiric corruption eat a world. He knows exactly where to plant it.
He has walked through every kind of ruin there is. He can still smell the corruption in each.
He knows which of them will matter later. He settles it now.
Generals die too. He has watched it happen in every ending.
He walks in through the gate they forgot to watch.
The whole camp, the same night.
A cut rope, a spooked horse, a missing quartermaster.
Half the counting-houses in the Empire owe him money from a life they cannot remember.
He has seen what the taint becomes. He burns it out early.
A fire in the right storehouse ends a siege early.
Every wall falls eventually. He only hurries it along.
A banner remembered is a banner that does not fall. Every army he has ever stood with fights harder for it.
Every door in the world has a friend on the inside, and he has met all of them.
Wherever he rests, someone leaves a light on. He has never asked them to.
Where others see scrub, he sees supper.
Their wounded do not come back to the line.
He knows the shortcut. He has walked it in three other lives.
He knows which roads will close, and which ships will sink.
He has walked this road in four endings. It never got shorter by itself.
He finds men to fill the gaps. He knows where they hide.
Nothing on a battlefield is wasted while he is there.
He knows where they are. He usually knows where they will be.
He reminds the people what the alternative looks like.
He has read books that have not been written yet. Theirs are easier.
He remembers which years the crops failed, and plants for them.
Half the captains of the world once sat at his table and listened.
He trains them for the war after this one.
Not a killing blow. A reminder.
He has all the time in the world. He has had it before.
The Winds do not rush through him anymore. They wait in him, patient, like water in a cistern.
He has learned to hold more of the Winds than a body should.
He stopped asking the Winds for power. Now he simply lets them through.
There is a pattern behind the pattern. He has seen it from the far side.
He has drunk from this well in lives that never were. The well recalls him kindly.
He knows exactly how a spell goes wrong, because he has watched it go wrong.
The Winds find him now. They have learned where he stands.
Anyone can pour more power in. He knows when to stop.
The words come faster each time. He has said them in every tongue that ever ended.
The Winds come easier to a mind with no fear left in it.
Just when the pool runs dry, he finds another cup behind it.
And then to pull it tight, to a point.
Every ending, the first thing he learned was to hold one thought steady while the world shook.
The same words, the same breath, every time. The Winds learn to expect it.
He learned to let the thread spread before it settles.
Men stand firm around someone who is not afraid. He stopped being afraid a long time ago.
The sea came in over the walls. He held a shield above his head for a long time.\\n\\nLocks the other Endings.
The sky burned for nine days and he watched it from the last tower. His blade remembers the heat.\\n\\nLocks the other Endings.
The granaries were empty before the first battle. He remembers what was worth taking.\\n\\nLocks the other Endings.
The cities emptied quietly. He learned what a slow death tastes like.\\n\\nLocks the other Endings.
Nobody screamed. The army simply stopped arriving. He keeps his own march quiet now.\\n\\nLocks the other Endings.
There is no error left for him to make. He made them all in other lives.
Everything he teaches, he learned the hard way. Several times.
He has watched this army walk into this ambush before. Not this time.
He has died before. He did not care for it, and he takes more killing now.

He has been a swordsman, a sorcerer, a spy and a steward, in one ending or another. This time he is all of them at once.\\n\\nA discipline counts once he knows 5 of its skills: Arts, Memory, Magic (learned spells count) and Hero work. Every discipline that counts makes him stronger, and all four make him the strongest he can be.\\n\\nLocks every Apex.
He is slow and he is soft, and he has made his peace with both. The wards take what the staff cannot turn.
He stops throwing the Winds and starts aiming them.
Every step he takes is slow, so he makes every step count from further away.
When they reach him anyway, the staff throws them back where they came from.
Small charms on every banner pole.
He cannot outrun anything, so they learn to stand where he cannot be reached.
He threads a ward through every rank before the first blow.
The staff drinks the Winds and gives them back to him, five bolts at a time.
Before the lines meet he walks along them and touches every blade.
He stands where the blows land thickest and lets them come.
He has watched too many men die to arrows to let it happen to him.
He was never quick. He learned to be hard to kill instead.
He does not move, and nothing moves him.
Men stand firm next to a man who will not step back.
He calls the volley before the archers loose.
Every shield overlaps the next, the way he showed them.
Not his god's faith. His own, that this time will be different.
Whoever stands behind him is out of reach. He has made sure of it in every world that ended.
He breathes out, and the arrow goes where he looked.
Sometimes the beast reaches him anyway. The knife was always for that.
He sees the shot before he takes it, and he packed for a long hunt.
One arrow, saved for the biggest thing on the field.
He shows the archers where to aim.
Every stone and stake is a range marker to him, and every cart carries spare shafts.
Archers near him shoot as if he were checking every shot.
He nocks six arrows at once. He learned it from a world where there was never time for one.
Nock, draw, loose. He counts it out until they no longer need him to.
A blow from above, with all of him behind it.
He stopped aiming at one man a long time ago.
One swing, three men. He has done the sums.
Every man in the arc gets the same chance. None of them like it.
He makes them practise until they stop flinching.
He goes first. They follow, and they keep swinging.
He teaches them where the armour is thinnest.
He stops choosing targets and lets the blade go round.
He knows what this battle will cost and pays it early.
The blade was made for one job: rider and horse, one stroke.
He finds the gap in a war beast's armour on the first try.
The heavy head keeps moving after the cut, and whatever stands in its arc goes down with it.
Monsters are only large men. He has the reach for them.
He teaches every unit where to stand when the big ones come.
Half the baggage, twice the marching. They arrive fresh.
Every plate has a seam. He shows them all of them.
He has seen this charge before, in a war nobody else remembers. It breaks on them.
The glaive line that stopped an empire's cavalry, as he remembers it, in one pair of hands.
Blows ring off him like a hammer off an anvil.
An open hand that lands with the weight of a falling ingot.
Each strike falls like the smith's hammer, and the men around the one he hits feel it too.
He takes the hit and does not move a step. Neither do the ones who stand with him.
He works them like iron, heat and blow, and every fight teaches them twice as much.
Broken units are mended and sent back to the line, harder than before.
New recruits are put next to his veterans from the first day, and they learn fast.
Every unit under him becomes the company he once led. They take a blow the way metal takes the hammer.
